transfer_scope: Reuse with retained context tests the frozen module plus Astra's planning, not the module alone.

steps.note: The arm is stationary and clear of the block; a small first-motor pulse will reveal its motion direction before building a feedback skill.
Positive motor 0 moved the tip left and up; an isolated motor 1 pulse will identify the second direction and coupling.
Both pulses increased their respective joint angles, with distinct tip directions; install goal-error feedback with joint damping for reusable tip positioning.
The block remains at +30 degrees; approach above its right end to prepare a clockwise rotating push.
The tip reached its goal accurately without contact; push down on the right end to reduce the block's positive yaw.
The downward push mostly translated the block and reduced yaw only 2.3 degrees; withdraw left above it to change the contact leverage.
The tip is clear to the left and the block is below the slot centerline; move below its left half for an upward, clockwise push.
The transit grazed the left corner and increased yaw to 46.7 degrees; the tip is now below it, so an upward push should reverse that rotation.
The upward push again acted near the end face and mostly translated; shift below the lower long edge to obtain a clockwise moment.
The lateral shift increased yaw to 54.8 degrees; push upward and left from this lower-right contact to reverse the torque.
End-face contact continues to translate with little rotation; retreat fully left before approaching the upper long side.
The retreat cleared the block without disturbing it; move above-left to contact the long side near its upper end.
The tip is above-left with clear space; drive diagonally right-down onto the upper long side for clockwise rotation.
Long-side contact rotated the block clockwise by 40.4 degrees; a small downward continuation should finish alignment and lower its center.
Yaw is now 1.2 degrees and the block nearly fits the slot height; withdraw upward to preserve alignment before moving behind it.
Withdrawal preserved the 1.1-degree alignment; move left above the block, avoiding another corner graze.
The tip is safely left of the block; descend behind its left face at the block center height.
The tip is centered behind the aligned block with no rail contact; begin a modest rightward insertion push.
The block advanced 2.45 cm into the mouth without rail contact and remains at 1.6 degrees; continue rightward while keeping the pusher centered.
Success is true: the block is fully inside, aligned at -1.9 degrees, and settled below the speed threshold.
The new yaw is -30 degrees, requiring counterclockwise rotation; approach above the left half rather than repeating the previous clockwise push.
The tip reached the upper-left approach without contact; push diagonally down-left onto the long side to turn the block counterclockwise.
The push corrected yaw to +2.7 degrees with only 3 mm translation; withdraw upward-left to preserve this alignment.
The block stayed aligned during withdrawal; descend safely behind its left face, matching the current center height.
The pusher is behind the block and its projected height fits the gap; push right to test entry while monitoring yaw and rail contact.
The block advanced 2.61 cm without rail contact and remains aligned at 3.6 degrees; continue insertion with a slightly higher centered push.
Success is true: the block is fully inside, aligned at -3.3 degrees, and settled below the speed threshold.
The block is at 30° and clear of the rails; a short motor-0 probe will identify its effect before controlled contact.
Motor 0 increased q0 with modest joint coupling and no block contact; probe motor 1 to establish the second control direction.
Both positive inputs increase their corresponding joint angles; install a damped, speed-limited Cartesian goal controller using the observed arm geometry.
The block remains at 30° without contact; approach above its right end to prepare a clockwise alignment push.
The tip reached above the right end without disturbing the block; push downward briefly to rotate it clockwise, then inspect displacement.
Contact translated the block down 4.9 mm but rotated it only 2.8°; shift the push toward its extreme right corner for greater clockwise leverage.
The corner push overshot alignment to −13.2°; withdraw rightward before approaching underneath to lift and counter-rotate the block.
The tip is clear and the block has settled at −13.4°; move below its right edge without crossing the block.
The tip passed below the block without contact; position slightly right of its center for an upward correcting push.
The tip is below and slightly right of center; an upward push should raise the block toward the slot center while correcting negative yaw.
The block is centered vertically but still at −11.6°; move along its underside toward the right corner to increase rotational leverage.
Yaw improved to −7.6°, within tolerance, and the block is centered; withdraw below it to reposition behind the left face.
The block remains settled and aligned within tolerance; traverse below it to reach the left-side approach corridor.
The tip is safely left of the block; raise it to the block centerline for a rightward insertion push.
The tip is on the centerline behind the block; push right toward the entrance and inspect any yaw or lateral drift before rail engagement.
The block advanced 24.6 mm with no rail contact and yaw −8.4°; continue along the slot centerline while monitoring clearance.
The block is nearly inside, with its rear edge still short of x=0.183; push another few millimeters while slightly lowering the contact line to improve yaw.
Success is true with the block fully inside at −7.8°; retract the pusher slightly to remove contact and let residual motion stop.
Success remains true after withdrawal: the block is fully inside, yaw is −7.8°, velocity is zero, and pusher contact is clear.
The new yaw is −30°, requiring counterclockwise rotation; approach above the left end for a downward corrective push.
The tip is above the left corner and clear of contact; press downward in a short step to measure counterclockwise rotation.
The push barely changed yaw because the tip slipped onto the left face; shift right and downward onto the upper-left corner to generate counterclockwise torque.
The contact is translating rather than rotating the block; withdraw above it to obtain a true top-face approach.
The upper-left corner is now near x=0.145; approach just to its right so downward contact acts on the top face rather than the end face.
Top-face contact corrected yaw by 17° with little translation; continue briefly to bring −12.5° nearer horizontal without overshooting.
Yaw is now −7.1° but the block is 10.7 mm below center; withdraw up-left to prepare a separate upward centering push.
The tip is clear to the left and yaw settled at −6.1°; move down the clear left corridor to reach the underside.
The tip is below the block with clear separation; move beneath its center, slightly rightward to preserve or improve alignment during lifting.
The tip is beneath the block near its center; push upward to remove the 10.7 mm vertical offset before insertion.
The block is now only 1 mm below center and yaw is −5.7°; withdraw downward to preserve this insertion-ready pose.
The block remains stationary and aligned after release; move below its left edge to set up the insertion approach.
The left-side corridor is clear; raise the tip to the block's center height for a balanced rightward push.
The tip is behind the left face at the correct height; advance toward the slot and check whether alignment survives first insertion.
The block advanced 22.9 mm without rail contact and remains at −6.7°; continue insertion at the same height until its rear edge clears the entrance.
Success is true with the block fully inside at −8.1°; retract leftward to release contact and verify a motionless final state.
Success remains true after release: the block is fully inside, yaw is −8.1°, velocity is zero, and pusher contact is clear.
